meta.title: Two Mornings, Two Emails
meta.textType: functional: two emails about daily routines

paragraphs: At lunch break on Monday, October twelfth, Lily and Leo sat at the library computer. Two emails were in the inbox. One was from Grace to Lily, and one was from Ravi to Leo. Last week, the two children asked their pen pals, "What is your morning like?" Now they had the answers. "Which email shall we read first?" asked Leo. "Grace's email is first," said Lily. Lily read it out loud.

"Dear Lily, thank you for your question about my morning. I get up at six o'clock when my alarm clock rings. Before school, I get dressed and eat toast. I prepare my school bag, too. I usually leave home at a quarter to seven. I take the bus at seven. My school starts at eight o'clock. I like my morning because it is quiet. What do you do in the morning? Best wishes, Grace."

Then Leo read Ravi's email. "Dear Leo, my morning is very early. I play badminton, so I wake up at half past five. My training is at a quarter past six. After training, I get dressed and eat breakfast. I usually wait at the bus stop at seven. I am always hungry at breakfast! It is a long morning, but I like it. Best wishes, Ravi."

"Ravi gets up earlier than I do!" said Leo. "I always get up at a quarter to seven." "His morning does not look like mine." "Grace gets up later than Ravi, but earlier than I do," said Lily. "Then I have the latest morning of all," said Leo. Lily wrote an answer to Grace. "Dear Grace, thank you for your email. I get up at a quarter past six, so my morning is later than yours. Best wishes, Lily." Before she sent it, Lily read it again. Then the bell rang, and lunch break ended. "Our mornings are different, but we are friends," she said.
text.summary: Lily and Leo read two emails from their pen pals about their mornings. Then they compare the times and write an answer.
